Adding to this confusion is evidence that "Genesis B" appears to be a translation from an earlier and separate Old Saxon retelling of the biblical "Book of Genesis", a fragment of which (corresponding to lines #791-817 of "Genesis B") survives.

arxiv-2006-11692.title: Semi-Supervised Object Detection with Sparsely Annotated Dataset
arxiv-2006-11692.creator: Jihun Yoon, Seungbum Hong, Sanha Jeong, Min-Kook Choi
arxiv-2006-11692.description: Abstract In training object detector based on convolutional neural networks, selection of effective positive examples for training is an important factor. However, when training an anchor-based detectors with sparse annotations on an image, effort to find effective positive examples can hinder training performance.

arxiv-2008-00469.title: A study of diffusion in network with multi-body interactions using Hypergraphs
arxiv-2008-00469.creator: Anirban Banerjee & \And Samiron Parui
arxiv-2008-00469.description: Abstract . Being cognizant of the abundance of multi-body interactions in various complex systems, here we investigate a possible way to incorporate multi-body interactions in dynamical networks. Adopting hypergraph as the underlying architecture aids our proposed dynamical network models to go beyond the traditional archetype of only pairwise interactions.

arxiv-2101-10194.title: Quantum Polarization of Qudit Channels
arxiv-2101-10194.creator: Ashutosh Goswami, Mehdi Mhalla, Valentin Savin, [2mm] Univ. Grenoble Alpes, Grenoble INP, LIG, F-38000 Grenoble, France
arxiv-2101-10194.description: Abstract We provide a generalization of quantum polar codes to quantum channels with qudit-input, achieving the symmetric coherent information of the channel. Our scheme relies on a channel combining and splitting construction, where a two-qudit unitary randomly chosen from a unitary 2-design is used to combine two instances of a qudit-input channel.

arxiv-2104-04969.title: Stability of Neutron Stars with Dark Matter Core Using Three Crustal Types and the Impact on Mass-Radius Relations
arxiv-2104-04969.creator: Adrian G. Abac, Christopher C. Bernido, Jose Perico H. Esguerra
arxiv-2104-04969.description: Abstract We investigate the effects of dark matter (DM) on the nuclear equation of state (EoS) and neutron star structure, in the relativistic mean field theory, both in the absence and presence of a crust. The σ − ω \sigma-\omega model is modified by adding a WIMP-DM component, which interacts with nucleonic matter through the Higgs portal.

arxiv-2207-13279.title: Comments on ”Imaging Reanalyses of EHT Data”
arxiv-2207-13279.creator: Makoto Miyoshi, Yoshiaki Kato, Junichiro Makino
arxiv-2207-13279.description: Abstract On June 14 2022, the EHT collaboration (hereafter EHTC) made the web page 1 1 1 https://eventhorizontelescope.org/blog/imaging-reanalyses-eht-data with the title ”Imaging Reanalyses of EHT Data”, in which they made comments on our recent paper Miyoshi et al. 2022 published in the Astrophysical Journal.

arxiv-2212-04804.title: Computationally accelerated experimental materials characterization - drawing inspiration from high-throughput simulation workflows
arxiv-2212-04804.creator: Markus Stricker, Lars Banko, Nik Sarazin, Niklas Siemer, Jan Janssen, Lei Zhang, Jörg Neugebauer, Alfred Ludwig
arxiv-2212-04804.description: Abstract Computational materials science increasingly benefits from data management, automation, and algorithm-based decision-making for the simulation of material properties and behavior. Experimental materials science also changes rapidly by incorporation of ‘machine learning’ in materials discovery campaigns. The obvious benefits which include automation, reproducibility, data provenance, and reusability of managed data, however, is not widely available in the experimental domain.

arxiv-2302-04598.title: Equivariant Euler characteristics on permutohedral varieties
arxiv-2302-04598.creator: Vincenzo Galgano, Hanieh Keneshlou, Mateusz Michałek
arxiv-2302-04598.description: Abstract By the work of J. Huh, one can interpret binomial coefficients as a solution to an intersection problem on a permutohedral variety X E X_{E} . Applying Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch, this intersection problem is equivalent to computing Euler characteristic of a specific element of K K -theory of X E X_{E} .

arxiv-2309-14853.title: Unipotent Representations of Complex Groups and Extended Sommers Duality
arxiv-2309-14853.creator: Lucas Mason-Brown, Dmytro Matvieievskyi, and Shilin Yu
arxiv-2309-14853.description: Abstract . Let G G be a complex reductive algebraic group. In [ LMM21 ] , we have defined a finite set of irreducible admissible representations of G G called unipotent representations , generalizing the special unipotent representations of Arthur ( [ Art83 ] ) and Barbasch-Vogan ( [ BV85 ] ).

arxiv-2501-02966.title: Human Gaze Boosts Object-Centered Representation Learning
arxiv-2501-02966.creator: Timothy Schaumlöffel *, Arthur Aubret *, Gemma Roig † \dagger, Jochen Triesch † \dagger
arxiv-2501-02966.description: Abstract Recent self-supervised learning (SSL) models trained on human-like egocentric visual inputs substantially underperform on image recognition tasks compared to humans. These models train on raw, uniform visual inputs collected from head-mounted cameras. This is different from humans, as the anatomical structure of the retina and visual cortex relatively amplifies the central visual information, i.e. around humans’ gaze location.

pmc-10542293.title: Simulation of the occipital transtentorial approach incorporating visualization of the cerebellar tentorium using three-dimensional computed tomography angiography and gadolinium-enhanced T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging: technical note
pmc-10542293.creator: Yuto Shingai, Masayuki Kanamori, Yoshiteru Shimoda, Shingo Kayano, Hitoshi Nemoto, Shunji Mugikura, Ryuta Saito, Teiji Tominaga
pmc-10542293.description: The occipital transtentorial approach (OTA) is one of the useful approaches to the lesions of the pineal region, dorsal brainstem, and supracerebellar region. However, a wide operative field is sometimes difficult to obtain due to the tentorial sinus and bridging veins. This study evaluated the usefulness of preoperative simulation of OTA, specifically including the cerebellar tentorium in 9 patients.

pmc-10555529.title: Influence of sexual dimorphism on satellite cell regulation and inflammatory response during skeletal muscle regeneration
pmc-10555529.creator: Charline Jomard, Julien Gondin
pmc-10555529.description: After injury, skeletal muscle regenerates thanks to the key role of satellite cells (SC). The regeneration process is supported and coordinated by other cell types among which immune cells. Among the mechanisms involved in skeletal muscle regeneration, a sexual dimorphism, involving sex hormones and more particularly estrogens, has been suggested.

pmc-11399603.title: Furin, ADAM, and γ-secretase: Core regulatory targets in the Notch pathway and the therapeutic potential for breast cancer
pmc-11399603.creator: Kuo Yao, Xiang-Yi Zhan, Mei Feng, Ke-Fan Yang, Ming-Sheng Zhou, Hui Jia
pmc-11399603.description: Highlights•Function of Notch pathways vary across subtypes of breast cancer.•Furin protease, ADAM, and γ-secretase are key targets for breast cancer treatment.•Positive cascade regulation between Furin protease, ADAM, and γ-secretase.•Potential targets of the Notch Pathway: O-fucosyltransferase, CSL and MAML. Introduction The Notch pathway plays an important biological role in the proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis of tumor cells.

pmc-11422222.title: Intermittent hypoxic training – derived exosomes in stroke rehabilitation
pmc-11422222.creator: Myoung-Gwi Ryou, Summer Burton
pmc-11422222.description: Ischemic stroke is the fourth leading cause of adult disability in the US, and it is a huge social burden all over the world. However, the efficient treatment of ischemic stroke is not available. An apparent reason for failing to find or develop an intervention for ischemic stroke is contributed to the tight blood–brain barrier (BBB).

pmc-11543637.title: WHO global research priorities for antimicrobial resistance in human health
pmc-11543637.creator: Silvia Bertagnolio, Zlatina Dobreva, Chad M Centner, Ioana Diana Olaru, Daniele Donà, Stefano Burzo, Benedikt D Huttner, Antoine Chaillon, Nebiat Gebreselassie, Teodora Wi, Mateusz Hasso-Agopsowicz, Benedetta Allegranzi, Hatim Sati, Verica Ivanovska, Kavita U Kothari, Hanan H Balkhy, Alessandro Cass
pmc-11543637.description: SummaryThe WHO research agenda for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in human health has identified 40 research priorities to be addressed by the year 2030. These priorities focus on bacterial and fungal pathogens of crucial importance in addressing AMR, including drug-resistant pathogens causing tuberculosis.

pmc-11642547.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Liver Lipidomics Signature in Adults with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis—A Pilot Study
pmc-11642547.creator: Thomai Mouskeftara, Georgios Kalopitas, Theodoros Liapikos, Konstantinos Arvanitakis, Eleni Theocharidou, Georgios Germanidis, Helen Gika, Giovanni Tarantino, Mariapia Vairetti, Andrea Ferrigno
pmc-11642547.description: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disorder in Western countries, encompassing a range of conditions from steatosis to Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH), which can potentially progress to cirrhosis. Lipidomics approaches have revealed significant alterations in the hepatic lipidome associated with both steatosis and steatohepatitis, with these changes correlating with disease manifestation.

pmc-11669302.title: Emergency Debulking of Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis: An Anesthesia Challenge
pmc-11669302.creator: Amit Padvi, Namita Padvi
pmc-11669302.description: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare condition involving the recurrent growth of benign papillomas in the respiratory tract caused exclusively by human papillomavirus (HPV). We present the case of a five-year-old child who arrived at the emergency department with severe respiratory distress, hoarseness, and biphasic stridor.

pmc-12397321.title: Computational insights and experimental breakthroughs in identifying next-generation acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
pmc-12397321.creator: Devaraj Hanumanthappa, Bandral Sunil Kumar, Sandra Ross Olakkengil Shajan, Nandini Markuli Sadashivappa, Shivaraj Kumar Walikar, Basavana Gowda Hosur Dinesh, Srinivas Ganjipete, Selvaraj Kunjiappan, Panneerselvam Theivendren, Kumarappan Chidamabaram, Damodar Nayak Ammunje, Parasuraman Pavadai
pmc-12397321.description: The study aimed to identify the potential acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors for effective Alzheimer’s treatment from existing FDA-approved drugs through a drug repurposing technique via computational tools. Further, to evaluate the anti-Alzheimer’s potency of the identified drug with the help of a suitable drug delivery system through in vivo pharmacological studies.

pmc-12604869.title: Association Between Resident Physicians’ Self-Rated Patient Care Ownership and Medical Professionalism Assessed by Patients: A Single-Center Study
pmc-12604869.creator: Hirohisa Fujikawa, Takuya Aoki, Daisuke Son, Masato Eto
pmc-12604869.description: IntroductionPatient care ownership (PCO) has received substantial attention as a core aspect of medical professionalism. In recent years, a quantitative PCO Scale (PCOS) has been developed and widely utilized. Despite its growing importance, PCOS is measured through resident physician self-assessment, and the association between PCOS scores and resident evaluation by patients, the primary stakeholders in clinical care, remains underexamined.

pmc-12751914.title: Prevalence of arrhythmias and associated factors among COVID-19 patients in the intensive care unit at COVID-19 treatment centers, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2022. A cross-sectional study
pmc-12751914.creator: Gobu Letemu, Zuriyash Mengistu, Emebet Berhane WoldeMariam
pmc-12751914.description: BackgroundCoronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), predominantly a respiratory illness, has been a global human threat that causes a multisystem disease, specifically cardiac arrhythmia commonly occurs. Currently, studies about the prevalence of Arrhythmias among COVID-19 patients are limited in low-income countries, including Ethiopia.ObjectiveTo assess the prevalence of arrhythmias and associated factors among COVID-19 patients in the ICU.

pmc-13040071.title: Subgenual anterior cingulate cortex in major depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis of MRI studies with patients and healthy controls
pmc-13040071.creator: Ilya Demchenko, Rachel L. Sousa-Ho, Vanessa A. Baltazar, Ishaan Tailor, Niloy Roy, Tom A. Schweizer, Sidney H. Kennedy, Alexandre Boutet, Andres M. Lozano, Katharine Dunlop, Venkat Bhat
pmc-13040071.description: BackgroundThis systematic review aims to synthesize anatomical and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings in the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) and associated network among medication-free patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) compared to healthy controls.MethodsA search for published studies was performed through Ovid (MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycINFO) on 18 April 2024.
